feed.title: Lupine Science
feed.subtitle: Lupine Science makes AI predictions for new materials trustworthy before a lab spends a year on them.

entry.title: Lupine Science is heading to TMS2027
entry.summary: Lupine Science will attend TMS2027 in Orlando, March 14–18, 2027. Alex Welcing will present an accepted poster on measuring the errors of interatomic potentials.

entry.title: What the Cap Was Hiding
entry.summary: A preregistered correction trial failed. Reopening the mathematics rather than the conclusion showed the gate was mis-tuned, the confirmatory test could not have passed even in principle, an escape statistic proposed as an input to the next round had no physical content, and the replacement gate carries a rounding hazard of its own. The license results are theorems in Lean 4; the rest is arithmetic replayed from the hash-locked records.

entry.title: Sharing DFT anchors reduces projected evaluations by 72.4%
entry.summary: Under the preregistered sparse-anchor rule, the locked Z1 records require 558 projected DFT evaluations when four model-specific anchor sets are counted separately and 154 when duplicate image indices are shared: 72.4% fewer DFT evaluations.

entry.title: The Small Cell Held: A 16-Element MLIP Elastic Benchmark
entry.summary: On this benchmark, the 1×1×1 TensorNet/PBE arm and the 3×3×3 reference arm have nearly identical elastic-constant error, while the tested global correction operator makes the result substantially worse.

entry.title: The Union Verdict: A De-brief on the Z1 Campaign
entry.summary: All four models scored strong-win on the same-engine gate, at a measured $14.65. The interesting parts are not the wins — they're the guidance split, the cost collapse, and what broke along the way.

entry.title: The Savings Stack: A Booklet on Doing Less, and the Commons That Makes Everyone Faster
entry.summary: The Savings Stack v1 release: a 16-page booklet on compute-savings in atomistic simulation — 72.4% fewer DFT evaluations when four models share anchors (558 naive vs 154 union, 29 paths, 3.62×), 163 citations verified, every number hashable and reproducible.

entry.title: An Order of Effort: Where Correction Laws Hold, and Where the Boundary Begins
entry.summary: We mapped the hard end first on purpose. Now the ladder is drawn: where our correction layer already wins, where only boundary theorems can speak, and the order of effort for the rounds ahead — each with its price list.

entry.title: The Z1 Barrier Panel: Evaluating Foundation MLIPs on 42 Solid-State Electrolyte Chemistries
entry.summary: Our barrier campaigns run on 42 published Li-ion electrolyte materials: 30 frozen test chemistries and 12 disjoint training chemistries. Here is what is in the panels and why these materials decide whether solid-state batteries ever ship.

entry.title: Four Gates, Three Honest Failures, One Live Experiment
entry.summary: Three of our four campaign gates have reported in, and all three are failures or abstentions — recorded, hash-locked, and explained. The fourth is running right now. This is what open-science instrumentation looks like when the answers are no.

entry.title: Beyond Carbon: The Error Geometry of Environmental Materials
entry.summary: The environmental-expansion series opens by establishing the correction-and-verification layer as a platform for any material whose function is controlled by under-coordinated environments.

entry.title: Cement, Concrete, and the Weight of the Built World
entry.summary: Cement decarbonization is a prediction-trust problem. Corrected universal machine-learning interatomic potentials apply directly to the disordered, under-coordinated materials in alternative binders, alternative clinkers, and CO₂-cured concrete.

entry.title: Critical Minerals, PFAS, and the Remediation Imperative
entry.summary: Critical-mineral recycling, direct lithium extraction, and PFAS destruction share a common materials-discovery problem: accurate binding and activation energies in under-coordinated environments, addressable by corrected uMLIPs and machine-checked verification.

entry.title: Methane and Refrigerants: Cutting the Non-CO₂ Climate Forcers
entry.summary: Methane and hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants are the largest non-CO₂ climate levers; both are materials-limited, and the correction-and-verification layer changes the discovery geometry.

entry.title: Water and Air: Correcting the Molecules Humans Drink and Breathe
entry.summary: Water and air quality depend on materials that separate and transform molecules in under-coordinated environments; the correction layer fixes the uMLIP errors that corrupt discovery of those materials.

entry.title: The Correction That Hurt, and the Theorem That Stopped It
entry.summary: Our first correction arm made alloy predictions worse; we turned the failure into a machine-checked law, explored a direction-gated rule that cut lattice errors 3–5×, and then let an adversarial review find where our own claims outran their licenses — those corrections are in this draft.

entry.title: Lupi Gains HFC Refrigerant Research Payloads
entry.summary: The latest Lupi viewer release adds R32 and R125 NVT simulations from the Maginn group force fields, a fix ave/chunk profile parser, vector glyph views, and billion-atom brick LOD.

entry.title: Non-CO₂ Climate Forcers, Now Formalized in Lean
entry.summary: The latest lupine-rhizo build adds ClimateForcers.lean and a validation module that machine-checks non-CO₂ warming potentials, lifetimes, and substitution savings — 899 theorems, zero sorry.

entry.title: A Field, Not a Neural Net
entry.summary: The largest errors in computational materials discovery have a low-dimensional geometry, and Lupine measures and corrects them at runtime with machine-checked proof.

entry.title: Five Materials That Could Unlock 5–12 GtCO₂/Year
entry.summary: Five computationally intractable materials—cobalt-free cathodes, halide solid electrolytes, MOF sorbents, ammonia catalysts, and lead-free perovskites—could unlock 5–12 GtCO₂/year, but only if the predictions sent to labs are corrected and verified first.

entry.title: From Predicted Crystal to Commercial Cell
entry.summary: A rigorous, partner-by-partner map from predicted crystal to commercial cell for batteries, carbon removal, ammonia, and solar absorbers.

entry.title: Investing in the Trust Layer
entry.summary: Why trust, not raw prediction volume, is the binding constraint in computational materials discovery, and how the Lupine Science correction-and-verification layer builds it.

entry.title: The 0.2% Synthesis Problem
entry.summary: A review of the 0.2% validation rate of structure-generation campaigns, the four structural filters that cause it, and the gigatonne-scale cost of leaving the problem unsolved.

entry.title: The Trust Layer
entry.summary: AI made imagination and simulation nearly free. Belief is now the bottleneck. The proof infrastructure for designed matter is being built in the open.

entry.title: A smooth, environment-resolved error field underlies the systematic property errors of universal machine-learned interatomic potentials
entry.summary: For fcc metals, uMLIP errors project onto a smooth field over local atomic environments. The field predicts a never-fitted property with r = 0.906, converts into a run-time correction, and carries machine-checked applicability boundaries.

entry.title: The Order Is Right, the Size Is Wrong
entry.summary: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (CHGNet, MACE-MP, MACE-MPA-0) measured across 21 materials and up to 9 properties against 228 published reference values

entry.title: Why LUPI?
entry.summary: LUPI as a live, install-free window into molecular structures and its implications for research, teaching, and public trust.

entry.title: Why Lupine Science?
entry.summary: Generative AI produces countless material candidates, but its simulations are wrong in structured ways; the bottleneck is not more models but makeability, and the response is machine-checkable certificates of synthesis, stability, and performance.

entry.title: From Fantasy Frameworks to Makeable Materials: A Prospectus for Formalized MOF Discovery
entry.summary: Theorem-proved certificates of synthesizability for AI-generated metal–organic frameworks, and a lab partnership to close the generate–test–learn loop.
